articles.title: Loan-Originating AIF framework
articles.requirement: Where an AIF originates loans as part of its strategy or has substantial loan-origination exposure, the AIFM must apply: a leverage cap of 175% (closed-ended LO-AIF) or 300% (open-ended LO-AIF) calculated on a commitment basis; single-borrower concentration limit of 20% NAV; a 5% retention obligation on transferred loans (with carve-outs); robust risk-management + liquidity-management policies + procedures; prohibition on originating loans to specified counterparties (the AIFM itself, the depositary, group entities).

articles.title: LO-AIF strategy + open-ended carve-outs
articles.requirement: An LO-AIF is (a) one whose investment strategy is mainly origination of loans, OR (b) one where the notional value of originated loans exceeds 50% of NAV. Open-ended LO-AIFs permitted only where the AIFM demonstrates the liquidity-management framework supports the redemption profile (ESMA RTS sets the specifics).

articles.title: LMT selection — minimum two
articles.requirement: Open-ended AIFs (and UCITS) must select at least 2 LMTs from the harmonised list (Annex V): redemption gates, redemption notice period extensions, redemption fees, swing pricing, dual pricing, anti-dilution levy, side pockets, suspension, redemption in kind. Money-market funds + open-ended LO-AIFs subject to specific selection rules.

articles.title: LMT activation governance + disclosure
articles.requirement: AIFMs (+ UCITS ManCos) must document procedural + governance arrangements for selecting + activating LMTs: triggers + criteria, approval authority, investor disclosure (prospectus + ad-hoc), CSSF notification (immediate for suspension / side pockets, periodic for other LMTs). Annual review of LMT framework.

articles.title: Delegation framework reform
articles.requirement: AIFMs must (a) ensure they retain substance + cannot become letter-box entities; (b) notify CSSF of all delegation arrangements (function, delegate identity, jurisdiction, sub-delegations); (c) demonstrate ongoing monitoring of delegates; (d) apply heightened scrutiny to portfolio + risk-management delegation outside the EU. CSSF Circular 18/698 expectations remain authoritative, supplemented by AIFMD II.

articles.title: Minimum substance requirement
articles.requirement: Each AIFM (and UCITS ManCo) must have at least 2 natural persons either resident in the Member State who are employed full-time by the AIFM, or members of the governing body of the AIFM who are committed to its activities + present in the Member State sufficiently to conduct effective decision-making. Reinforces the existing Lux 'conducting officer' framework.

articles.title: Retail marketing of AIFs — harmonised framework
articles.requirement: Where Member State law permits AIF marketing to retail investors, AIFMs marketing must provide retail-appropriate disclosures (KID/PRIIPS-equivalent), apply suitability or appropriateness assessment per MiFID/PRIIPS principles, and follow the same conduct-of-business standards as for professional clients (where applicable). In Luxembourg, Part II UCIs continue to be the typical retail-permitted AIF vehicle.

articles.title: Expanded supervisory reporting
articles.requirement: AIFMs report to CSSF + ESMA on a periodic basis covering: leverage methods + ratios; LMT selections + activations; delegation chain detail; loan-origination concentration (for LO-AIFs); sustainability-risk integration; ICT-risk integration; key risks managed. ESMA technical standards specify the report format; CSSF Circular 25/901 operationalises for Luxembourg.

articles.title: Supervisory cooperation + ESMA powers
articles.requirement: ESMA's coordination role expanded — peer reviews + comparative analyses of national authorisation + supervisory practices; specific powers on LMT activation oversight; cross-border enforcement coordination. Reduces forum-shopping risk for AIFMs structuring across Member States.

articles.title: Depositary cooperation + reporting
articles.requirement: Depositary obligations clarified: must cooperate with AIFM + delegates; report concerns to CSSF directly where AIFM failures detected; specific obligations on cash-flow monitoring + safekeeping of crypto-assets where AIF holds them. Depositary agreement must be updated to reflect AIFMD II amendments.

articles.title: UCITS amendments — LMT alignment
articles.requirement: UCITS Directive amended to require UCITS ManCos to select + operate LMTs on the same basis as AIFMs. CSSF expectations: UCITS prospectus updates by 16 April 2026 to disclose selected LMTs; governance framework parity with AIF process.

articles.title: UCITS amendments — delegation parity
articles.requirement: Delegation provisions aligned with AIFMD II — letter-box prohibition, notification, sub-delegation transparency. Applies equally to UCITS ManCos as to AIFMs.

articles.title: LO-AIF risk-management framework
articles.requirement: AIFMs of LO-AIFs must implement specific risk-management policies + procedures covering: credit + concentration risk; valuation of loans; recovery + collateral; conflict-of-interest avoidance (where the AIFM also originates loans for related parties); stress-testing of credit + liquidity scenarios; independent review by risk-management function.

articles.title: LO-AIF liquidity-management framework
articles.requirement: AIFMs of open-ended LO-AIFs must implement specific liquidity-management procedures: cash + cash-equivalent buffers; modelling of loan cash flows; restrictions on redemption frequency reflecting underlying loan tenor; stress-testing under multiple redemption + drawdown scenarios; LMT activation framework specifically calibrated for credit-fund vehicles.
